rubrics.date: Rubricae generales 10–12 and 15–17 (Vatican typical edition, p. [XII]), with the table at 91 (places 14–17), 93 and 95 (p. XVII): a second-class Sunday is preferred to a second-class feast of the universal Church that is not a feast of the Lord (16), and the feast so impeded is not transferred but commemorated or omitted according to the rubrics (93, 95); a first-class Sunday is preferred to every feast (15), and a feast of the Lord takes a second-class Sunday's place (16 a, 17). The Mass of the Sunday within the octave of the Nativity commemorates the occurring feast of the second class and not the octave (Vatican p. 22).
rubrics.scope: Observed in the Mass of the second-class Sunday by the impeded feast's own Collect, Secret and Postcommunion, as the feast's formulary assembles them; in the commemoration of the Chair of St Peter, St Paul's oration follows St Peter's at once and the two count as one (Rubricae generales 110, p. XVIII).
rubrics.rank: Rubricae generales 106–109 (p. XVIII): the commemoration of a second-class feast is ordinary (109), made in every low Mass and in a sung conventual Mass, and omitted in a sung Mass that is not conventual (108).
rubrics.admission: Rubricae generales 111 a–b and 434 a–b (pp. XVIII, XXXI): a second-class Sunday admits one commemoration, that of a second-class feast, which is omitted when a privileged commemoration is to be made; a first-class day, and a sung Mass that is not conventual, admit only one privileged commemoration; 113–114 (p. XIX): a de Tempore commemoration comes first and the excess is omitted.
rubrics.conclusion: Rubricae generales 436–437 (p. XXXI): each commemoration oration follows the corresponding Mass oration under its own, separate conclusion; 480–481: only the last Secret's terminal is audible.
